idea-plugin.name: mlab security
idea-plugin.description:
CVE scanning for your lockfiles, powered by mlab. Right-click a lockfile, get its known vulnerabilities with exploitation intelligence, and see them in the Problems view.

Features

  • Check for Lock Vulnerabilities on any supported lockfile, from the Project view, the editor or the Tools | mlab menu, or scan every lockfile in the project at once.
  • A report tab with a per-severity verdict, CVSS, EPSS and CISA / EU known-exploited status for every advisory, sorted by real exploitation before CVSS band.
  • An mlab tool window listing findings by lockfile and severity, and vulnerable lockfiles colored in the Project view by their worst severity.
  • An inspection reporting each advisory on the line that declares the package.
  • Quick documentation on any CVE identifier, in any file: CVSS, EPSS, known-exploited status, weaknesses.
  • Analyze Selection: look up a selected URL, IP, email, file hash, MAC address or domain.
  • Automatic rescans when a lockfile changes, cached per content so an unchanged file is never re-uploaded.

Supported lockfiles: Cargo.lock, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, composer.lock, Gemfile.lock, go.sum, requirements.txt, mise.lock.

Data and privacy

  • Nothing is uploaded until you agree. The first scan asks for consent. Opening a project makes no network call.
  • A scan uploads only the lockfile you scan to vuln.mlab.sh (or your self-hosted endpoint), never your source code.
  • CVE details send only the CVE identifier. Analyze Selection sends only the selected value, to the mlab platform endpoint for its type. A domain lookup is the one kind that contacts the target.
  • API credentials are kept in the IDE password safe only. No telemetry is collected.
  • Scanning and lookups are disabled in untrusted projects.

Anonymous scans are limited to 8 per hour; a free token from vuln.mlab.sh raises this to 25.
